title: Evolutionary conservation of MECP2 and its relevance to neuronal stability and behavioral adaptation
title_zh: MECP2的进化保守性及其对神经元稳定性和行为适应的意义
abstract: MECP2 encodes a methyl-DNA-binding chromatin protein whose dosage is critical for nervous system function: loss-of-function variants cause Rett syndrome, whereas increased dosage causes MECP2 duplication syndrome. Despite extensive research on MECP2 in neurodevelopmental diseases, its unexplored evolutionary history, which we derived from comparative genomic analysis of hundreds of species, provides a novel evolutionary framework for understanding the profound consequences of MECP2 perturbation on brain and behavior. In this review, we analyze the phylogenetic profile of MECP2 and discuss how comparative, molecular, and developmental evidence supports the idea that MECP2 gained significant importance in vertebrate nervous systems. This is because broad CpG methylation, postnatal accumulation of neuronal non-CpG methylation, and long-lived post-mitotic circuits created a growing need for stable yet flexible interpretation of methylation states. We further discuss evidence that MECP2 is functionally anchored to a conserved chromatin-repression axis, particularly the NCoR/SMRT corepressor machinery, while also showing signs of more lineage-restricted integration with mammalian dosage-sensitive regulatory networks. We propose that MECP2 is best understood as a vertebrate-specialized regulator that helps preserve transcriptional homeostasis in mature neurons while allowing experience-dependent plasticity. This framework links methylome interpretation to behavioral adaptation and may help explain why MECP2 dysregulation produces such profound and dosage-sensitive consequences for brain function and behavior.
abstract_zh: MECP2编码一种甲基化DNA结合的染色质蛋白，其剂量对神经系统功能至关重要：功能缺失变异导致雷特综合征，而剂量增加则导致MECP2重复综合征。尽管对MECP2在神经发育疾病中的研究已相当深入，但其尚未被探讨的进化历史——我们通过对数百种物种的比较基因组分析得出——为理解MECP2扰动对大脑和行为产生深远影响提供了新的进化框架。在本综述中，我们分析了MECP2的系统发育特征，并讨论了比较、分子和发育证据如何支持MECP2在脊椎动物神经系统中获得显著重要性的观点。这是因为广泛的CpG甲基化、出生后神经元非CpG甲基化的积累以及长期存活的后分裂电路共同创造了对稳定而灵活解释甲基化状态的日益增长需求。我们进一步讨论了MECP2在功能上与保守的染色质抑制轴（尤其是NCoR/SMRT共抑制因子机制）相连的证据，同时也显示出与哺乳动物剂量敏感调控网络更具谱系限制的整合迹象。我们提出，MECP2最好被理解为一种脊椎动物专门化的调节因子，它帮助在成熟神经元中维持转录稳态，同时允许基于经验的可塑性。该框架将甲基组解释与行为适应联系起来，可能有助于解释为何MECP2失调会对大脑功能和行为产生如此深刻且剂量敏感的后果。
